Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’m using the `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill because this task changes a multi-wake target policy. I’ll first read the workspace contract, then the skill instructions and the current rollout evidence before touching the solver candidate or guidance.

The skill requires anchoring the keyframes to scores, observations, metrics, and diagnostics. I’ve confirmed that requirement; next I’m inventorying all sampled examples and inherited logs so the diagnosis uses the full allowed evidence set.

All four sampled keyframe sheets are byte-identical, despite three distinct policy sources; their reported rollout outcomes are also identical apart from bookkeeping. I’ll therefore inspect the shared sheet once and the released sheet once, then treat the four samples as one duplicated current rollout—not as four independent confirmations.

The visual and diagnostics agree: the fish actively travels about `4.68L` upstream and reaches `6.61L`, but then pitches into a large nose-up return and exits before entering the useful near-target wake corridor. The current terminal allocation reduces anterior speed/load (`251.35 deg/time`, RMS moment `985`) yet does not change that topology, so I’m now checking the documented state interface for a distinct recovery signal that stays inactive during the closing leg.

The skill’s evidence gate is satisfied. I’m recording the diagnosis and a single falsifiable hypothesis now, before any policy change: preserve the locally bracketed `0.10/0.65` terminal allocation and test the previously harmful `0.35` lateral-velocity correction only behind the existing rearward-plus-dual-opening selector, bounded to `2°` and still inside the `12°` steering ceiling.

The single candidate and durable lesson are now in place. The policy change is confined to two owned parameters and one gated steering term; the evidence lesson records why further terminal-allocation tuning is exhausted. I’m checking the exact diff and then invoking the mandated workspace check runner—without running CFD.

The guidance check passed. The mandated Julia contract command could not start because this environment has no `julia` executable on `PATH` (exit 127); that is an environment availability issue, not a policy assertion failure. I’m continuing with the required boundary/schema guard and will also run a local static field-contract check.

The provenance check exposed nested inherited optimizer notes that the shallow inventory missed. I’m reading those now to verify the chosen mechanism against the actual prior hypotheses—not just their distilled guidance—and will revise if they contradict this gated test.

The inherited provenance changes the decision: the immediately preceding gated lateral-motion candidate was already evaluated and was negative (`-11.1768`, `-4.637L` head-x, `9.365/9.295L` mean/final range), and terminal anterior speed protection was negative too (`-11.2587`). I’m retracting the duplicate hypothesis in the notes before changing the policy again. The replacement will test total terminal mean-curvature rolloff—distinct from joint-allocation interpolation, speed clipping, and motion feedback—while leaving the closing law algebraically unchanged.

The corrected candidate now rolls terminal steering authority to a `0.25` residual only after the strict rearward/dual-opening gate; it no longer repeats the evaluated lateral-feedback policy. The durable guidance now records both inherited step-19 negatives and tells later workers to avoid them. I’m rerunning every available check against this final version.

Final verification is clean for every check available here: guidance PASS, parameter ownership PASS (`23` referenced fields, all declared), editable boundary PASS, and no trailing whitespace. The Julia assertion remains unavailable because `julia` is not installed/on `PATH`; no CFD was run.

Produced exactly one multi-wake candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:17) applies gated terminal steering rolloff while preserving the evaluated closing law.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) records the evidence and falsifiable hypothesis.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:126) now records the terminal-allocation bracket and negative gated speed/lateral-feedback results.

Guidance, parameter-schema, and editable-boundary checks pass. Julia was unavailable on `PATH`, so its dynamic assertion could not run. No CFD was run.
